points: Lane: one piece of work, done by one builder on its own branch and folder.
Batch, or integration branch: several finished lanes merged together into one PR, so CI runs once.
Debt: a known gap, written down so it gets fixed. Note: a gap unlikely to matter, kept as one line.
Decision record: a file holding one ruling you made, and its reason.
Guard: a hook that checks each command or edit before it runs, and blocks it or asks you.
Gate or lint: a check that runs on files or in CI and fails when a rule is broken.
Worktree: a second copy of a repo in its own folder, so parallel agents don't collide.
Janitor or sweep: the script that removes finished worktrees and branches.
Design token: a named value such as --space-3 or --accent, used instead of a raw number. (A model token is different: a chunk of text, which is how usage is counted.)
Path-scoped rule: an instruction file that loads only when Claude touches matching files.
Sandbox: a fence the operating system puts around shell commands: which files and websites they can reach.
Deny rule: a settings line that blocks a command or file pattern in every permission mode.
Bypass mode: no permission prompts at all; only deny rules, hooks and the sandbox still stop anything.
MCP server or connector: a plug-in that gives Claude tools for an outside service, such as GitHub or a browser.
Mutation test: breaking a guard on purpose to prove its test notices.
Mockup: a picture of a screen, made before building it.
Artifact: a hosted page Claude publishes, like this roadmap.
Compaction: when a long session's history is summarized to fit; early details can fade.
Handoff: the file a session writes so its work survives compaction or a restart.
Dispatcher: one hook process that runs several checks in turn, instead of one process per check.
Exec form: a hook started directly from its command and arguments, with no shell in between.
'if' filter: a pattern on a hook, such as Edit(*.md), that Claude Code checks before starting the hook at all.
Http hook: a hook that posts to a small local server instead of starting a process.

claude -p: Claude Code run as a one-shot command (p for print): one prompt in, one answer out, then it exits. Hooks use it to ask a model in the background, and each one is a whole separate Claude Code process.
